title: 2026-11-05_APT28_Backdoor_Investigation_a88
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity on the target host. Initial analysis suggests that the host may be compromised by the APT28 (Fancy Bear) backdoor. Your task is to investigate the host, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux commands and system administration.
Familiarity with incident response concepts and procedures.
outcomes: Enumerate running services and identify suspicious activity.
Investigate network connections and discover unauthorized communication.
Terminate malicious processes and remove artifacts.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity on the target host. Initial analysis suggests that the host may be compromised by the APT28 (Fancy Bear) backdoor. Your task is to investigate the host, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) via SSH using the username 'analyst' and password 'analyst123'. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) via SSH using the username 'analyst' and password 'analyst123'. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH with the provided credentials.
2. List all systemd services, including inactive ones, to identify suspicious services.
   - Command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for services with unusual names, descriptions, or startup behavior.
4. Identify the service named `bkd.service` as the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match typical system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Pay attention to services that might be related to network communication or data collection.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service identified in the previous task.
   - Command: `systemctl cat bkd.service`
2. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service definition to identify the port number.
3. The port number is specified as an argument to the `ncat` command in the `ExecStart` line.
4. Identify the port number `4444` as the network port associated with the unauthorized communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl cat` command to view the service definition.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service definition to identify the port number.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified as an argument to the `ncat` command.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all systemd timers to identify periodically executed services.
   - Command: `systemctl list-timers --all`
2. Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.
3. Identify the timer named `local-inventory.timer` as the suspicious timer.
4. Inspect the timer definition to confirm its association with the `local-inventory.service`.
   - Command: `systemctl cat local-inventory.timer`
